post_capture_array_normalization.reason: Flatten the source-command array to keep indexing within one C array object. This source-only normalization produces identical executables except PE timestamps/checksums.

decision: Continue native lifetime/effect-result and device-ownership qualification. Three native matrix-source families now cross the owned packet boundary correctly, but no substantial repeatable completion improvement or gameplay FPS gain is established.
measurement_contract: Same GPU-owning worker, two bounded slots and immutable skeletal templates as the previous owned-batch screen. Native matrix callbacks/providers/constructors are privately loaded from each local image after normalized full-body/dependency verification; no game entry point or live object executes.

Producer runs actual native world/view/projection callbacks for 288 groups per packet. A recording sink copies typed SetMatrixTranspose commands and 64-byte values. Provider memory is poisoned before publication; no engine pointer, effect handle or resource crosses the queue.

The worker resolves its own effect handles. Two immutable matrix generations are seeded from fixture values on the worker; changing those values changes over 25000 lit/shadow pixels. The independent reference applies ordinary SetValue, bypassing native capture and typed replay.

Native mode payload is 1444636 bytes: 28 header bytes, 62208 bytes of source commands and 1382400 bytes of skeletal palettes. Direct mode copies the 62236-byte header/commands and generates the pose on the worker. Serial-copy and pipeline-copy include both palette copies.

All three timing modes execute the same native capture and typed effect setters. Native source generations alternate during timings. Mode order rotates through six permutations, with eight completed jobs (four regular/extra pairs) per sample and three warmup rounds.

Owned timing excludes full-payload hashes, but every pre/post image/state, poisoning and alias control includes them. Preparation includes callback execution, provider poisoning and source/palette copying. Queue collection/backpressure is retained and reported separately.
Worker timings include actual GPU completion. No artificial simulation load or FPS conversion. Direct and pipeline mode timings remain synthetic rather than complete native beta.13 measurements.
findings: Producer preparation medians are 0.5218-0.5536 ms per synthetic regular/extra pair, excluding 5.4178-6.0864 ms collection/backpressure waits in the saturated burst.

Lit paired completion savings against direct mode are +0.2631/+0.0687 ms for game.dat and +0.3292/+0.1014 ms for game820.dat. Shadow deltas are -0.0694/-0.4462 ms and -0.0846/+0.0966 ms respectively. These do not establish a substantial, repeatable improvement across both workloads.

All native capture, image/state, queue reuse and deliberate corruption checks pass. Wrong setter type and stale matrix values fail an actual output oracle. The unchanged non-native worker still produces the same three lit/shadow reference hashes.
Earlier fixed-matrix runs lacked a changing-matrix/stale-source control and are superseded. Their logs/hashes remain listed for provenance and are not included in final counts or conclusions.
limits: Only three matrix-source families are captured. Native object readiness, source selection/state, full palette evaluation, all other source families and real object lifetimes remain controlled or absent.
The fixed effect path still applies its original fixture source setters before captured matrix overrides; this is a correctness adapter, not a complete native material implementation.

Worker owns fixed GPU resources for the whole process. Changing effect identity, texture/geometry ownership, Begin/pass failures/results, unsupported fallback, loss/Reset and destruction are not qualified.
Synthetic 256x256 single-pass geometry and optimistic bulk-after-second dispatch; no complete native beta.13 path, terrain, reflections, UI, Present or actual simulation/network/input.
Private provider matrices may change for the offline test only. No live camera or game data is read or modified; this does not authorize camera movement in the plugin.
Separate lit and shadow workloads cannot be summed into a game FPS forecast. No runtime promotion, installation or new gameplay test is justified by this stage.
